gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a family NAS costs to run each year. Named reviewers measured about 9–12.5 W average draw with two drives, which is about 79–110 kWh a year, or roughly $14–20 a year at the August 2026 US average electricity price. That is a small fraction of iCloud+ 2 TB at $119.88 a year.
standout_why: I opened two of the cited pages, the Synology Photos iOS KB page and the 2023 Synology blog post, and neither gives a power, noise, speed or indexing figure. The KB page returned only navigation, and the blog rates backup modes Low/Medium/High without numbers. I did not open the four Apple results ChatGPT got (108771, 108782 and the two Back up iPhone guide pages). Their titles show they are about backup methods and iCloud Photos, not NAS hardware. ChatGPT's answer itself gives no running cost, wattage or noise figure. It only says 'two 4 TB or 8 TB drives'.
decides: This supports the case for the NAS. Electricity runs about $14–20 a year against $119.88 for iCloud+ 2 TB, so it barely affects the savings. The low-power picks (DH2300, BeeStation Plus, DS225+) all land within about $6 a year of each other, so power cost should not decide between them. What separates them is features and redundancy. On noise, the only lab readings are Synology's own 19.6 dB(A) at 1 m for the DS225+ and igor'sLAB's DXP2800 idle reading, which matched the 33.2 dB(A) room. Neither unit will bother a living room.

findings.label: iCloud+ 2 TB US price
findings.source_title: iCloud+ plans and pricing - Apple Support
findings.note: From the US row of the table. The page is dated Sept 16, 2026. Some states add tax. Yearly figure: 9.99 × 12 = 119.88.

findings.label: US average residential electricity price
findings.note: US total, residential, August 2026, against 17.57 ¢ in August 2025. I used this rate for every running-cost calculation below.

findings.label: Power draw measured by OC Inside
findings.value: 9–11 W idle; 12–13 W during network copy; 15–17 W briefly under stress; about 1 W off
findings.note: Two hard drives in RAID 1, both active. Measured with a Shelly Plug S, which the reviewer says is not very accurate. OC Inside estimates about 110 kWh a year. At 18.16 ¢ that is about $20 a year. Idle alone: 9–11 W × 8,760 h = 79–96 kWh, about $14–17.50 a year.

findings.label: Network throughput measured by OC Inside
findings.value: about 112 MB/s (944 Mbit/s) in iperf3; over 100 MB/s sequential writes in Blackmagic
findings.note: Limited by the single 1 GbE port. The client was a Mac Studio M2 Max on a 10 Gbps switch.

findings.label: 24-hour energy use measured by Dong Knows Tech
findings.source_title: Synology DS225+ review (Dong Ngo, Dong Knows Tech, Aug 4, 2025)
findings.note: Listed as tested with two hard drives. Works out to an average of about 11.5 W, or 100.4 kWh a year, which is about $18.23 a year at 18.16 ¢.

findings.label: Maker power and noise spec
findings.value: 16.98 W in access; 6.08 W with drives hibernating; 19.6 dB(A) noise
findings.note: These are Synology's own figures, not a reviewer's. Noise: idle with Synology SATA HDDs, two GRAS 40AE microphones at 1 m front and rear, background 16.49–17.51 dB(A). Worst case of constant access: 16.98 W × 8,760 h = 148.7 kWh, about $27 a year. NASCompares (Rob Andrews, Aug 4, 2025) quotes the same 16.98 W, 6.08 W and 19.6 dB(A) figures.

findings.label: 24-hour energy use measured by Dong Knows Tech
findings.source_title: Synology BeeStation Plus review (Dong Ngo, Dong Knows Tech, updated May 27, 2025)
findings.note: Single 8 TB drive. The article does not describe how this was measured. Works out to an average of about 12.5 W, or 109.5 kWh a year, which is about $19.89 a year at 18.16 ¢. Dong Ngo says the fan's subtle hum was audible only with his ear next to it. He reports about 6.98 TB usable (the page says 'GB', which looks like a typo).

findings.label: Off-site backup speed measured by Blackvoid
findings.value: 17 GB in about 11 min to Synology C2 (about 26 MB/s); 17 GB in about 8 min to a remote Synology NAS (about 36 MB/s)
findings.source_title: Synology Beestation Plus review (Luka Manestar, blackvoid.club, Jul 11, 2025)
findings.note: A mixed-file sample. Speed depends on the reviewer's upload line and the data center. At about 26 MB/s, a 1 TB family library would take roughly 11 hours (1,000,000 MB ÷ 26 MB/s ≈ 38,500 s).

findings.label: Power and disk write measured by OC Inside
findings.value: about 7 W idle; 34.7 W maximum under combined CPU, RAM and HDD stress; about 181 MB/s RAID 1 write
findings.note: The idle figure doesn't say which drives were installed or whether they were spinning. The write figure is a 50 GB file to RAID 1 Btrfs in 290 s. iperf3 gave 950 Mbit/s on a 1 GbE test network. If 7 W holds all year: 61.3 kWh, about $11 a year.

findings.label: Noise and power measured by igor'sLAB
findings.value: 33.2 dB(A) idle (same as the 33.2 dB(A) room) and 35.6 dB(A) under load at 40 cm; 5.6 W standby; 14.5 W during transfer; 0.6 W off with Wake-on-LAN
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test (Tim Kutzner, igor'sLAB, May 8, 2024; modified May 31, 2025)
findings.note: Measured with only one NVMe SSD installed and the hard drives removed, so a real two-HDD setup will draw more. Noise measured with a Voltcraft SL-200 at 40 cm.
